subject: Simple relation conditions
notes: Equal-length comparison in all three of its parts: equality when every pair matches (pb297 T01/T02/T03/T07/T12), the first unequal pair deciding (T15 differs at position 1, T11 at position 1), and the higher-collating operand being the greater one (T09 U+00FF over the low value; T08 shows two equal operands are neither less nor greater). The 2002 golden runs the same determination under a non-native PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE (U01-U03). WHICH OPERANDS REACH THIS RULE is now observed too, and that is what the prior evidence missed: the sentence says an alphanumeric operand may be compared 'to another operand treated as class alphanumeric for the purposes of comparison', which 8.8.4.2.5 makes a numeric integer operand compared with an alphanumeric one - and no golden held a numeric item, so a regression that answered such a relation WITHOUT the program collating sequence was invisible to the corpus (kb/Work PB741; NIST NC215A SEQ-TEST-GF-6/-7 was the sole witness). pb297 U11-U16 add the numeric anchor - LOW-VALUE, an ALL literal, the alphanumeric-literal twin that must agree, a signed anchor (14.9.25.4 GR6a drops the operational sign through 8.8.4.2.5's move) and a four-digit anchor - and the unit drift test pins the whole category matrix, so the numeric-vs-alphanumeric selection cannot silently become a numeric comparison again. The 'two zero-length operands are equal' sentence is pinned by conformance:cases/7.3.23-REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH/ref_mod_zero_length, not here.
